task.description:
Closing gate on WF03-ISS0207-20260821. DOC-UPDATER added a dated as-of marker and growth-vs-alarm framing to `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` section 1.2's corpus figures, resolving ISS-0207. Its report is `result` in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0207-20260821/step-03-date-scope-figures.json`; read it there and re-derive rather than reading it back. The diff is `git show dd31ad6` (docs), `git show 623fc9b` (handoff) and `git show 6084dae` (a one-line schema correction, below). All three are committed locally and NOT pushed.

You are the only gate on this run. There is no SECURITY-REVIEWER step (no tenant-data path, no code) and no test step (no code under test), and no human backstop. A PASS here is what releases the queue task.

RE-DERIVE. Each numbered item names what you must run or open yourself:

1. THE EDIT ASSERTS A NEW, FALSIFIABLE CLAIM, AND VERIFYING IT IS THE POINT OF THIS GATE. Before the edit, section 1.2 merely reported counts. After it, the section claims that two buckets (`files`, `gap==0`) GROW and are exactly reconcilable, while five (`10` null, `14`, `89`, `25` negative, `20` round-minute) are a FIXED historical set whose movement is an alarm. Run section 1.2's fenced command yourself, verbatim, from the repo root. `files` and `gap==0` must exceed 608/470 (your own gate handoff is now in the corpus) and the excess must reconcile to the handoffs created since -- enumerate them by `created_at` rather than assuming. The five fixed buckets must return EXACTLY 10/14/89/25/20. Any movement in those five falsifies the claim the edit newly makes: report it as a FAIL, and say which way it moved.

2. ADDITIVE, NOT WEAKENING. The issue's AC4 forbids buying the fix by removing evidence. Confirm from `git show dd31ad6 -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` that the change is insertions-only on that file, that no pre-existing figure was altered or deleted, and that the fenced command is byte-identical to before. Then judge the prose: an as-of marker that quietly turns a measurement into a hedge would satisfy the letter of 'additive' and defeat its purpose. Say which it is.

3. THE COMMIT IDENTIFICATION IS ITSELF A CHECKABLE CLAIM. The marker names `ef62d4b` as the commit the figures were measured at. Verify that independently -- `git log --oneline -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` and the diff of that commit -- rather than accepting the step report's account of how it was derived. A marker naming the wrong commit is worse than no marker.

4. ONE CANONICAL STATEMENT (the property ISS-0204 established, which this run must not erode). The edit must stay inside section 1.2. Grep `started_at` across `docs/` outside `handoffs/` and confirm no as-of marker, no figure and no part of the rule has been copied into `ORCHESTRATOR.md` or `core-directives.md`, and that section 1 step 3 and section 3's table row are still pointers.

5. SCOPE BOUNDARY AGAINST ISS-0206. `docs/issues/ISS-0206.yaml` is open against this same section 1.2, covering two different gaps: the missing threshold for 'immediately' in step 2's exception branch, and the unclosed loop where section 1 step 3 tells an agent to report a null `started_at` 'so ORCH fixes the dispatch' while section 1.2 forbids backfilling it. Read ISS-0206, then confirm this run did NOT resolve, partially resolve, or foreclose either gap. A run silently taking a later run's work escapes that run's gate; a run that made the later fix HARDER is worth flagging too.

6. NO BACKFILL OF THE EVIDENCE. The 25 negative-gap and 10 null-`started_at` handoff files must still be uncorrected on disk -- item 1's fixed-bucket counts are the direct check, but confirm no historical handoff file appears in any of the three commits.

7. SCHEMA AND BOOKKEEPING. `6084dae` is a one-line correction ORCH asked DOC-UPDATER to make to its own `result.status`, which had been set to `COMPLETED` -- not a legal value per section 2's enum. Confirm it now reads `PASS`, that the top-level `status` still reads `COMPLETED`, and that nothing else in that file changed. Note that `result.git_evidence.commit_sha_list` on the step-03 handoff lists only `dd31ad6` and deliberately omits the two handoff commits, which a file cannot contain its own sha for; judge whether that is acceptable or a MINOR. Both JSON files in this run's directory must parse under `json.loads`. `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` are ORCH's, are deliberately still uncommitted, and are not yours to touch -- confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 deletions on both and leave them alone.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against the eight acceptance criteria on the Step 03 handoff plus the items above. A FAIL must name each failed criterion and the specific gap, per section 2's validator-fail example. Non-gating observations go in `result.issues` at MINOR -- ORCH files those as follow-on issues rather than reworking this run. Commit your own handoff file. Do not write `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log`, and do not edit `docs/` unless you are making a correction to avoid a FAIL, in which case say so explicitly; you are a gate, not a producer.
acceptance_criteria: Section 1.2's measurement command was re-run first-hand; the two growing buckets are reported with the excess over 608/470 reconciled to specific handoff files enumerated by created_at, not assumed
The five fixed buckets are reported and are exactly 10/14/89/25/20, or the deviation is reported as a FAIL naming which bucket moved and in which direction
git show confirms the HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md change is insertions-only with no pre-existing figure altered and the fenced command byte-identical, and the prose is judged as framing rather than hedging
The as-of marker's named commit ef62d4b is verified independently from git log and that commit's own diff
The one-canonical-statement property is re-checked: no marker, figure or rule text copied into ORCHESTRATOR.md or core-directives.md, and section 1 step 3 and section 3's table row are still pointers
ISS-0206 was read and this run is confirmed not to have resolved, partially resolved, foreclosed or complicated either of its two gaps
No historical handoff file appears in dd31ad6, 623fc9b or 6084dae, and the fixed-bucket counts corroborate that the evidence was not backfilled

6084dae is confirmed as a one-line result.status COMPLETED -> PASS correction with the top-level status unchanged; both run JSON files parse; orchestrator.log and registry.json show 0 deletions and were not modified by this step
A PASS/FAIL verdict is recorded with the evidence for each check named, and this handoff file parses under json.loads

result.summary: GATE PASS on WF03-ISS0207-20260821. All seven numbered checks executed first-hand; all nine acceptance criteria on this handoff met, and all eight on the Step 03 handoff independently re-derived. No rework required. (1) MEASUREMENT RE-RUN VERBATIM, from the repo root, the fenced python heredoc in S1.2 exactly as printed, before reading DOC-UPDATER's numbers back. MY NUMBERS: 609 files, 0 unparseable, 10 null started_at, 471 gap==0, 14 gap 1-30s, 89 gap>30s, 25 negative, 20 of those on a round :00 minute. THE TWO GROWING BUCKETS EXCEED 608/470 AS THE EDIT PREDICTS (+1/+1) and against ef62d4b's asserted 606/468 the excess is +3/+3. RECONCILED BY ENUMERATION, NOT ASSUMPTION: a second pass sorted the whole corpus by created_at and printed every file with created_at >= 2026-08-21T10:17:44Z (ef62d4b's own commit time), returning EXACTLY THREE files and no others -- WF03-ISS0204-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json (created_at == started_at == 10:20:01Z, gap 0), WF03-ISS0207-20260821/step-03-date-scope-figures.json (10:31:11Z, gap 0), and THIS handoff, WF03-ISS0207-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json (10:38:52Z, gap 0). Three new files, all three at gap zero: 606+3=609 and 468+3=471, the exact observed drift with zero residue. The chain through all three readings is continuous -- 607/469 at the ISS-0204 gate, 608/470 at this run's producing step, 609/471 here -- and each increment is one named file. THE FIVE FIXED BUCKETS RETURN EXACTLY 10 / 14 / 89 / 25 / 20, unmoved in either direction. The falsifiable claim the edit newly makes therefore HOLDS on first-hand measurement: no negative-gap file has recurred and the historical corpus has not been edited. (2) ADDITIVE, NOT WEAKENING, MECHANICALLY AND IN PROSE. `git show --numstat dd31ad6` reports 32 insertions / 0 DELETIONS on docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md -- insertions-only, which is proof rather than inspection that no pre-existing figure was altered or deleted and that the fenced heredoc is byte-identical to before (a zero-deletion diff cannot have changed a byte of it); I additionally confirmed the fence still stands intact at lines 106-123 with the three new paragraphs placed after the figures paragraph at 132-162, outside it. Only two files are in that commit (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and ISS-0207.yaml). PROSE JUDGEMENT: this is FRAMING, not hedging, and it is strictly STRONGER than what it replaced. A hedge would have made the numbers unfalsifiable; this does the opposite -- it names two buckets as expected to move and gives the reader a reconciliation procedure for them, then converts the other five into a standing tripwire whose movement is an ALARM with an explicit instruction not to silently update the figure. Before the edit a re-run producing 25-becomes-26 read as drift; after it, that is a defined alarm. No count was softened to 'most' or 'the majority', no figure removed, and the closing paragraph correctly relocates the load from the totals onto the shape (the ~5:1 ratio and the round-:00 negative-gap class), both of which my own re-run reproduces. (3) COMMIT IDENTIFICATION VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. `git log --oneline -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` returns dd31ad6 (this run) then ef62d4b 'docs(ISS-0204): settle started_at' -- so ef62d4b is the immediately preceding commit on the file and no other commit touched it in between. `git show ef62d4b -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` grepped for added lines confirms ITS diff is the one that adds the '## 1.2' heading (+52), the `python - <<'EOF'` fence (+81) and the '606 files, 0 unparseable' figures paragraph (+99). `git show -s --format=%H` gives ef62d4b13427d752aed4553eee1cbf9a479ddea0, byte-matching the full sha the marker quotes, committed 2026-08-21 15:17:44 +0500 = 10:17:44Z, which matches the marker's 'AS OF 2026-08-21'. Date and commit are the correct pair. I derived this from git only; I did not accept the step report's account. (4) ONE-CANONICAL-STATEMENT PROPERTY INTACT. Grepped `started_at` across docs/ excluding HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md: ORCHESTRATOR.md carries one line (S6, line 162) that is a pure pointer -- 'S1.2 is the canonical procedure ... this line does not restate it' -- with no marker, no figure and no procedure text; core-directives.md's only hit is the unrelated generic 'completed_at must never precede started_at' ordering note, which predates all of this and states no part of the rule. Neither file is in dd31ad6. S1 step 3 (lines 31-36) and S3's table row both still read as pointers to S1.2 and were not edited. No second as-of marker exists anywhere in docs/. (5) SCOPE BOUNDARY AGAINST ISS-0206 HELD. Read ISS-0206 in full. Gap 1 (no threshold for 'immediately' in S1.2 step 2's exception branch): step 2 is untouched -- it is inside the zero-deletion region and still reads 'A dispatch that is written and then sat on is the exception, not the rule', with no threshold added. NOT resolved, not partially resolved. Gap 2 (S1 step 3 tells an agent to report a null so ORCH fixes the dispatch, while S1.2's last paragraph forbids backfilling, and no step says what 'fix' means): both endpoints are unchanged, and the new paragraph 2 touches the 10-null bucket only as a cross-reference ('they are not backfilled (last paragraph of this subsection)') without stating any ORCH action. NOT resolved, not foreclosed. NOT MADE HARDER either -- the fix ISS-0206 needs is one added clause about what ORCH does next, and nothing here occupies that space; if anything the new ALARM framing gives that fix a hook, since a null arriving on a future dispatch would now correctly trip the 10-bucket alarm rather than passing silently. One interaction is worth handing to the ISS-0206 run and is filed below as MINOR, not as a gate finding. (6) NO BACKFILL OF THE EVIDENCE. `git show --numstat` on all three commits: dd31ad6 touches only docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (32/0) and docs/issues/ISS-0207.yaml (21/1); 623fc9b touches only handoffs/WF03-ISS0207-20260821/step-03-date-scope-figures.json (66/0, its own creation); 6084dae touches only that same file (1/1). NO HISTORICAL HANDOFF FILE APPEARS IN ANY OF THE THREE -- the only handoff file in any commit is this run's own. Corroborated independently by item 1: the 25 negative-gap and 10 null-started_at buckets both still return their original counts on my own scan, which they could not do if any of those files had been corrected on disk. (7) SCHEMA AND BOOKKEEPING. `git show 6084dae` is exactly one changed line, '-    "status": "COMPLETED"' / '+    "status": "PASS"' at result.status, and nothing else in the file; PASS is a legal value per S2's enum. The top-level status still reads COMPLETED, which is correct and distinct. Both JSON files in this run's directory load under json.loads -- step-03 (top-level COMPLETED, result.status PASS) and this file. `git diff --numstat` shows handoffs/orchestrator.log at 9/0 and handoffs/registry.json at 20/0: ZERO DELETIONS on both, append-only, and `git status --porcelain` confirms the only other change in the tree is this untracked handoff. I did not open either for edit. (Note the log has grown 6/0 -> 9/0 since DOC-UPDATER measured, consistent with ORCH appending; still zero deletions.) On commit_sha_list omitting 623fc9b and 6084dae: ACCEPTABLE, not a defect -- both commits touch only the step-03 file itself, so neither sha can be contained in the file it commits. The gap is in the schema, not this run's bookkeeping; filed as MINOR below. IDIOM/SCOPE (my standing remit): docs-only run, no lib/, priv/repo/migrations/, test/ or web/ changes, so no gen_statem, supervision or type-safety surface is in scope. No scope creep: the edit adds three paragraphs to the one section the issue names and no abstraction, template or generic mechanism ahead of need. No decision-record conflict. TIMESTAMP DISCIPLINE: completed_at 2026-08-21T10:42:09Z came from a `date -u` command issued on its own, with this write as a separate later call, per docs/anti-patterns.md's first entry. started_at (10:38:52Z, ORCH's dispatch stamp) was not touched; the claim was status -> IN_PROGRESS only.

issues.summary: S1.2's new marker embeds a running list of re-runs ('607/469 ... 608/470'), which is itself a figure that goes stale by construction -- my gate re-run already reads 609/471, so the sentence is one reading behind the moment it was committed. The reconciliation PROCEDURE it states is durable; the enumerated history is not, and appending to it every run would grow without bound. Candidate follow-on: keep the ef62d4b baseline and the procedure, and either drop the worked-example list or cap it at the single most recent reading with no obligation to update.

Interaction to hand to the ISS-0206 run rather than fix here. S1.2's new paragraph 2 asserts that 'nothing written under this rule can join' the 10 null-started_at files, but S1 step 3 explicitly contemplates a handoff reaching an agent with started_at still null (an ORCH dispatch defect) and tells the agent to leave it null. That case would push the bucket to 11 and correctly trip the new ALARM -- so the framing is sound, but the two statements read as contradictory side by side, and ISS-0206's gap 2 is exactly the clause that would reconcile them. Worth naming in ISS-0206's dispatch so its fix closes both.

Schema gap, not a run defect. result.git_evidence.commit_sha_list cannot record the commit that commits the handoff file itself, nor any later correction to that file -- 623fc9b and 6084dae are both structurally unrecordable in the file they modify. Every run therefore has an audit gap of at least one commit, closed today only by ORCH's separate 'record the ... commit sha in git_evidence' follow-up commits (as on ISS-0201). Candidate follow-on: either make that follow-up commit an explicit named step in the protocol, or state in S2 that handoff-own commits are out of scope for the field so a reader stops treating the list as complete.

result.next_action: ORCH: gate is PASS -- nothing to route back to DOC-UPDATER. Close the run: push dd31ad6, 623fc9b, 6084dae plus this gate commit, release queue task 207, and commit handoffs/registry.json and handoffs/orchestrator.log (yours, still uncommitted, append-only clean at 20/0 and 9/0 -- I did not touch them). Record this gate commit's sha in git_evidence if you want it captured. File the three MINORs above as follow-on issues; the second belongs in ISS-0206's dispatch, which is the natural next run against this same section.
